solution: The given equations can be written as \(2x + 3y = 9\) and \(-x + y = -2\). Hence the matrix equation is \(\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 3 \\ -1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 9 \\ -2 \end{bmatrix}\) (i.e. \(AX = B\)). Now use \(R_2 \to 2R_2 + R_1\); we get \(\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 5 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 9 \\ 5 \end{bmatrix}\). We rewrite the equations as \(2x + 3y = 9\) ... (i) and \(5y = 5\) ... (ii). From (ii) \(y = 1\) and using (i) we get \(x = 3\). Hence \(x = 3,\ y = 1\) is the required solution.
note: The second equation is -x + y = -2, so the right-hand side is (9, -2), printed (9, 5); x = 3, y = 1 unchanged.
